claim: tweenPaths' subdivideTo spreads every segment length into Math.max, which throws on a large contour and is quadratic below that
roundRectPath writes duplicate consecutive points when the radius is half a side (pill shapes)

triage.scenario: `roundRectPath(0, 0, 40, 20, 10)` clamps the radius to 10 = height/2. The right corners' arcs then end and start at the same point (x+w, y+r): the top-right arc's last sample and the bottom-right arc's first sample. The path gets a zero-length `L` at each side that has no straight run. A stroked pill marker then has degenerate segments, where join and miter math has no direction to work from. The answer should skip a corner's first sample when it equals the previous corner's last.
triage.cause: every corner emits both of its end samples, even when the straight run between corners has no length

claim: mergeRegion's welder can map the same point to two different welded points, so a contour's last end and first start come apart

triage.scenario: the welder answers the first stored point within `snap` that it meets while walking the 3×3 cells in a fixed order. It does not answer the first point stored. A contour's start S is welded once, at its first segment, onto A. Later, B is stored: B is more than `snap` from A but within `snap` of S (A and B can be up to 2·snap apart). When the contour's last segment ends at S, the welder can meet B's cell before A's and send S to B. The first segment then starts at A and the last ends at B, so the ring no longer closes. `flattenAll` splits it into separate open rings, which throws off the winding counts, and `chain` leaves a gap that `emit` closes with a stray edge. This needs contours with near-coincident corners, which is exactly the case welding is there for.
triage.cause: welds to the first match in cell order, not the first point stored (or the nearest), and keeps no memo per input point

claim: schneiderFit breaks the tangent at every split, so a fitted pencil stroke has a corner at each joint
spiroToPath drops `closed` on a two-point contour, so reading the path back reopens it
reachToMeet with an explicit `maxDistance: Infinity` in tangent or eased mode meets nothing
resamplePath's 10,000-anchor cap on spacing counts pieces rather than anchors, so the cap does not limit anchors as intended

triage.scenario: a path of many open subpaths with a small `spacing`: the check sums `span.pieces`, but each open subpath writes `pieces + 1` anchors, and one-anchor subpaths add their anchors too. A path of 2,000 open two-anchor subpaths at a spacing giving 5 pieces each sums to 10,000 pieces and passes, writing 12,000 anchors, past the cap the option documents ("A spacing that would place more than 10,000 anchors places 10,000"). The count branch does count fixed anchors (`fixedCount`), so the two branches answer the cap differently.
triage.cause: spacing branch compares piece total, not anchor total

claim: joinPaths drops every part's `corners` and `openFill`
tugPathEnd keeps the end anchor's dangling handle on a straight extension piece, so the straight run comes out curved

triage.scenario: `tugPathEnd(set, { sub, end: 'first' }, 40, 'tangent')` on an `AnchorSet` whose first anchor carries an `inHandle` (a pen-drawn set where the first point was dragged, or a last anchor holding an `outHandle`). `atTail` reverses the subpath, so that `inHandle` becomes the tail anchor's `outHandle`. `growTail` only lengthens in place when the last segment is straight; otherwise `appendPieces` pushes the line piece and assigns handles only when `pts.length === 4`. The stale `outHandle` stays on `prev`, so `isStraightSegment(prev, next)` is false and the new segment is drawn as a cubic shaped by that handle. It should be a straight line along the tangent. On a cusp anchor whose dangling handle points off the tangent, the extension visibly bends. Any mode whose first piece is a line takes this path: `'tangent'` always, and `'curvature'` or `'eased'` on an end with no bend.
triage.cause: line piece leaves prev.outHandle untouched

claim: joinPaths measures every part from the first part's origin, so a far part joined after a near one loses its float32 precision
snipPathAt removes two pieces when the probe's nearest point is exactly a crossing, and a closed subpath crossed once comes back in `removed` drawn twice
mergeRegion can leave a ring open where three edges cross at one point, and emit then closes it with a chord
where: packages/geom/src/paths/mergeRegion.ts:54-56 (crossingPoint per pair), :232 (cutSegment skips a cut within 1e-9 of the last), :320-344 (chain), :355 (emit closes)

claim: reachToMeet and extensionPieces use different tests for a straight 'curvature' end, so a near-straight end with no maxDistance extends as a huge full circle

triage.scenario: With no `maxDistance` in 'curvature' mode, `reachToMeet` sets `reach = Infinity` whenever `frame.curvature !== 0`. `extensionPieces` decides "bends" by `|κ|·distance > STRAIGHT_TURN` (pathEndExtension.ts:71), and with an infinite distance that test passes for any nonzero κ. A curved end that is straight up to float32 noise (say a segment `convertSegments` turned into a curve with handles at thirds, then stored as float32, giving κ ≈ 1e-12) gets four quarter-circle cubics of radius ~1e12. The crossing with a boundary 100 units ahead then sits at `ta` ≈ 1e-10 on a cubic whose control points are 1e12 away, where `segmentCrossings` and `pieceLengthAt` lose precision or miss the hit. The same end with any finite `maxDistance` is grown as a straight line. The straightness decision should be one test, the `STRAIGHT_TURN` one, used in both places.
triage.cause: two straightness tests (`!== 0` vs `STRAIGHT_TURN`)

claim: resamplePath allocates pieces with no bound, so a small `spacing` (or a huge `count`) hangs
`mergeRegion` throws when a long straight edge has a short, slightly tilted one lying along it
simplifyAnchorsAt rotates a closed subpath so it starts on a different anchor
pathToD writes no moveto for a subpath that opens without one, so its output draws nothing

triage.scenario: a `PolygonPath` whose command stream starts with a drawing command (`[PATH_L, PATH_L]`, coords `[10,0, 10,10]`). `forEachSegment` and every other reader in geom treat it as a subpath opened at the pen, stored (0, 0), which is `origin` in the path's own space. pathToD emits `L10 0L10 10`. SVG data that does not open with a moveto is in error and renders nothing, and `pathFromD` of that string returns an empty path. The round trip loses the whole path. Expected: an `M` at the implied pen, i.e. `M{origin.x} {origin.y}` (0 0 when the path has no origin), before the first drawing command. `PathBuilder` always emits the `M`, so only paths built from raw command arrays reach this.
triage.cause: implicit subpath opening not lowered

claim: resamplePath with a NaN tolerance halves every piece down to the subdivision limit

triage.scenario: `opts.tolerance` is NaN, e.g. from an emptied numeric field. `Math.max(NaN, 1e-6)` is NaN, so `worst(...) <= tol` and `err > tol` are both false. No piece is ever taken as straight. The halving test `err > tol` is false too, so pieces are not halved either: every piece is fitted as a cubic, including runs that are dead straight, and their anchors gain handles. A finite tolerance keeps straight runs as lines. The fallback should treat a tolerance that is not a finite positive number as the default 0.5, the way `count` already does.
triage.cause: NaN tolerance not defaulted

claim: `roughenPath` gives two contours the same offsets once a contour has more than 65,536 samples
splitByClosure gives corner specs to the wrong anchors after a subpath that starts without an M
roundRectPath with cornerSamples 0, and circlePath with segments 0, build NaN or empty geometry
mergeRegion with `tolerance: 0` drops every piece and returns an empty path
pathFromD draws the path after an unknown leading command instead of drawing nothing

triage.scenario: `pathFromD('X M0 0 L10 0')`: `strayPathDataHead` passes (the head is a letter), the unknown `X` is warned about and skipped with `continue`, and the `M`/`L` that follow are drawn. SVG treats an unknown command as an error and renders the path only up to it, so here nothing should be drawn; the same applies mid-path, where SVG stops at the bad letter and this keeps going. This contradicts the function's own rule elsewhere ("a command with the wrong number of arguments ends the path before it, as SVG renders both").
triage.cause: unknown command skipped (`continue`) rather than ending the path (`break`)

claim: splitSubpaths omits the implied moveto when the path's first subpath opens without one

triage.scenario: The doc promises that every drawing command that opens a subpath without an `M` "gets the `M` it implies". `pen` is only set when a boundary is crossed with `i > cmdStart`. At `i === 0` the condition is false, so for commands `[L, L, Z, M, L, Z]` the first returned subpath is `[L, L, Z]` with no `M` and its `sources` has no -1 entry. Drawn alone that is fine, but a consumer that reorders or joins the parts (for example `joinPaths(splitSubpaths(p).reverse())`, or `splitByClosure` when that subpath ends up after another in its group) draws it from the previous subpath's pen, not from (0, 0).
triage.cause: `i > cmdStart` guard skips index 0

claim: pathSignedArea returns a negative area for a RectPath with negative extent, contradicting "counts as positive"
`pathFromD` ignores numbers after `Z` and keeps drawing, where SVG stops at the error
Synthesizing the move for an implicit subpath after close spreads the entire command and coordinate streams into constructor calls, throwing past the argument limit on large inputs
mergeRegion runs quadratically in segment count: overlapCuts tests every segment pair and filledSide computes a full winding for each piece

triage.scenario: a flattened outline of 20,000 straight edges (a traced bitmap, a densely sampled freehand fill) runs `endsAlong` on every pair of line segments (~2·10^8 calls, each allocating arrays), then `winding` walks every ring point twice for every piece. The call blocks for many seconds where a bounding-box prefilter (as `crossingsAmong` presumably has) would make it near-linear.
triage.cause: no spatial prefilter on pairwise overlap test or winding probe

claim: Curvature-mode tug tests a straight end with curvature === 0 while the extension uses a turn threshold, so a near-straight end is handled inconsistently

triage.scenario: a curved end whose curvature is float noise rather than zero. One example: a segment turned into a curve by `convertSegments` (handles at the thirds, then stored as float32, so the cross product reads ~1e-12 instead of 0). With `mode: 'curvature'` and no `maxDistance`, `reachToMeet` sets `reach = Infinity` because `frame.curvature !== 0`. `extensionPieces(frame, Infinity, 'curvature')` then passes its own `|k|·distance > 1e-6` test and draws a full circle of radius ~1e12, in quarter-circle cubics whose chords are ~1e12 long. Crossings with a stroke 100 units ahead fall at t ≈ 1e-10 on such a piece, and the distance read from them (`pieceLengthAt` × a piece length of ~1.6e12) carries an absolute error far larger than the geometry. `lengthToward` takes the same branch and measures by angle about a center ~1e12 away, where `atan2` of the cancelling cross and dot products loses most of its digits. What should happen: the end is treated as straight, as `extensionPieces` itself would treat it for any finite distance, so reach is bounded by the strokes' extent and the length is a plain projection.
triage.cause: straightness decided two ways (exact zero vs STRAIGHT_TURN)

claim: pathFromD draws a path from data that does not begin with a moveto when numbers come before the first letter
Identity affine fast path adds width to the translated x before differencing, so a rect at x=2**54 with width 1 comes out with width 0
Marker builders write absolute float32 coords with no origin, so a marker far from 0 loses its shape
solveSpiro forces the tangent at a point next to a coincident neighbor to +X
reachToMeet skips crossings with the end's own last segment, so a reach that meets that segment finds no crossing

triage.scenario: an open path whose last segment is a cubic hooked so its end's extension (tangent, circle of curvature, or eased spiral) runs back across that same segment, e.g. a curvature-mode reach on a curled end, where the circle of curvature follows the last segment back around → the whole end segment is dropped from the candidate strokes, so the first real crossing is missed and the end reaches past it to a further stroke, or returns null. The touch at the end itself, the reason for dropping the segment, is already handled by the `touching` threshold in `reachToMeet`.
triage.cause: whole segment excluded instead of only its touch at d≈0

claim: An out-of-range number in non-arc path data is dropped and the following arguments slide into its slot

triage.scenario: `pathFromD('M0 0 L1e400 5 10 10')` → `readNumbers` skips `1e400` (Infinity) and returns `[5, 10, 10]`, so `pathFromD` draws `L5 10` and then stops at the odd argument. Every coordinate after the bad number moves one slot over, so the path is drawn with wrong geometry instead of stopping where the error is. `readArcArgs` already ends the run at such a number; `readNumbers` should do the same (stop, not skip), so the command counts as short and the path ends before it, as SVG does.
triage.cause: skip instead of stop on a non-finite token

claim: reachToMeet finds the crossing on one cubic approximation of the arc but places the end on another, so the end lands off the stroke

triage.scenario: `mode: 'curvature'` (or `'eased'`) end with a large radius, e.g. r = 1000, boundary crossed partway round. The search builds `extensionPieces(frame, reach, ...)`: for an unbounded reach that is one full turn in four quarter cubics, each up to ~2.7e-4·r off the true circle. It records `best`, the cubic arc length to the crossing. `tugOpenEnd(path, end, best)` then rebuilds the arc for `best` alone, with a different piece count, and its end point is computed exactly on the circle (`at(i * step)`). That point is not where the search's cubic crossed the boundary: for r = 1000 it can be ~0.27 units off, either short of the stroke (a visible gap) or past it. A second Reach then finds the same stroke a sliver away (beyond `touching`) and adds another tiny piece. `'eased'` has the same shape of error: `fitSpiral` refits the drawn stretch for each distance, within `FIT_SHARE · ease`.
triage.cause: crossing measured on one approximation, end placed by another

claim: mergeRegion leaves a gap mid-contour where two or more consecutive sub-`snap` straight edges are dropped, and the merged output gains chords across the shape
reachToMeet in `'curvature'` mode on a straight end, with no `maxDistance`, grows an infinitely long line and finds nothing
simplifySpan returns one anchor for a run of coincident anchors, so simplifyAnchorsAt deletes the run's last anchor

triage.scenario: a run of three or more selected anchors that all sit on one point (stacked by a snap): every `sampleRun` dedupes to one point, `fitStops` adds nothing, and `result` is just the first anchor, with the last anchor's outHandle copied onto it. simplifyAnchorsAt sees `refit.length < end - start + 1` and splices, removing the run's last anchor, which the doc says always stays, and its inHandle is lost.
triage.cause: no guard that the refit still ends on the run's last anchor

claim: mergeRegion reads its winding from a fill-dependent area while treating every subpath as closed
tweenPaths drops a contour that has no segments on one side, so at(1) is not the second shape

triage.scenario: `a` holds a bare `M` subpath (a lone pen point), which `pathToCubicContours` gives as a contour with no segments, while `b`'s matching contour has k segments. `collapsed()` only runs when the contour is missing altogether (`ca[i] ?? …`), not when it is empty, so `matchContours` calls `subdivideTo([], k)`, which returns `[]` (`segs.length === 0` early return). `lerpContour` maps over `a.segs`, so the result has no segments for every `t`, including `t = 1`, contradicting "exactly the second at 1". Expected: an empty contour is treated like a missing one (grown from a point via `collapsed`).
triage.cause: empty contour not routed to `collapsed`

claim: `simplifyPath` drops lone-anchor subpaths, though its doc says open ends stay
pathInWorld can return the input Path instance instead of the fresh Path it promises

triage.scenario: when the path's AABB already equals the pose box and the pose has no rotation or transform, `pathInPoseBox` returns `path` itself and `pathInWorld` returns `local` unchanged, so `pathInWorld(p, pose) === p`. The docstring says "Returns a fresh `Path` instance; never mutates inputs", so a caller that trusts it and edits the result in place (for example, writing into `coords`) mutates the stored path.
triage.cause: docstring contradicts the identity shortcut

claim: simplifyPath leaves a duplicate seam anchor on a closed subpath when its last corner-to-corner run collapses to one point

triage.scenario: a closed subpath with corners where the final run (last corner back to `corners[0] + n`) has coincident anchors, e.g. the last anchor duplicated on the first. `sampleRun` dedupes it to one point, the loop `continue`s, so no run is ever fitted with `last = true`; the run before it was fitted with `last = false` and pushed its end anchor, which sits on `out[0]`. The closed result then carries two anchors at one point (a zero-length closing segment) instead of closing on `out[0]`.
triage.cause: `last` keyed on the run's position, not on the last run actually fitted

claim: zigzagPath never pushes the leading points when a contour starts on a zero-length segment

triage.scenario: a contour whose first segment has no length, e.g. `M0 0 L0 0 L10 0 L10 10 Z` (a doubled anchor, which happens when a pen click lands twice). Each sample on that segment has `dir === null`, and `normal` starts as `{0, 0}`, so the first `pieces` points get no offset and sit on the outline, breaking the alternation the docs promise. The comment says such a point "keeps the one before's normal", but the first points have no point before them. Those leading points should take the first non-null normal in the contour.
triage.cause: normal seeded with zero instead of the first defined direction

claim: translatePath leaves a far-moved origin-free polygon in raw float32, where transformPath gives it an origin
pointAlongPath with t = NaN returns a NaN station instead of a clamped one

triage.scenario: `Math.min(Math.max(NaN, 0), 1)` is NaN, so `measure.at(NaN)` runs. In `at`, `target` is NaN too, `segmentAt` falls back to segment 0, and `pointOnSegmentOnly` is evaluated at NaN, giving `{x: NaN, y: NaN}`. The doc says `t` is clamped to 0..1. A NaN fraction can come from a 0/0 ratio upstream, such as a zero-length drag. The same gap exists in `PathMeasure.at`'s own clamp (pathMeasure.ts:146).
triage.cause: Math.min/Math.max let NaN through

claim: roughenPath's seed is truncated to an int32, so fractional seeds all roughen the same way
pathDistanceToPoint measures a negative-size RectPath as if the point were outside it
simplifyPath with a NaN tolerance drops straight segments

triage.scenario: `resamplePath(p, { tolerance: NaN })` (an unparsed field from a panel): `Math.max(NaN, 1e-6)` is NaN, so `worst(...) <= tol` and `err > tol` are both false. fitPiece never accepts the straight answer, never halves, and always emits a cubic, fine; but in simplifyPath the same NaN reaches `sampleRun`, where `Math.min(8, Math.max(1, Math.floor(len / (4 * NaN))))` is NaN and the `k <= steps` loop adds no samples for any straight segment, so straight runs fit as though their far anchors did not exist. Should fall back to the default the way a non-finite `count` does.
triage.cause: `Math.max` with NaN propagates NaN; no finiteness check
